chapter: Chicago radio, Whiteman and courting Mildred
title: Mildred's temper, divorce and happy early marriage
summary: Dance asks about Mildred's rages; Norvo says they were happy, and that Whiteman let her fly to the coast for her divorce.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Well listen, you'll have to tell me -- if you say I shouldn't talk about it. Since you remember perfectly well that Mildred and I were good pals, and I remember her very well getting mad and cussing and scaring everybody to death all the time, was she always like that?
Like what?
Well you know -- how Mildred was. She'd fly into -- she rather be dying laughing or flying into a rage at somebody. Or something. Am I wrong?
No, not at the beginning, no. I think as it went along --
Did she get more like that?
Actually, she was -- I enjoyed being around Mildred.
Oh, yeah.
We were very happy for a long while.
She was wonderful company.
OH, yeah, we got along fine. I -- we had no problem. And Mildred was very considerate, too, I think. Ah --
She was very understanding, wasn't she?
Yeah. Course when I first went with Mildred, she was married. She hadn't got her divorce yet.
Oh, she hadn't. Oh, I see.
So, Whiteman let her off in Chicago. She flew out to the Coast --
Oh.
-- got a divorce, he let her off.
She'd been separated from him for some- time and --
Oh, yeah. She'd been separated from -- for a long while but --
Oh. But --
But never divorced.
Yeah.
And so it was more so when she went -- when she went with Paul, back East.
Yeah, yeah.
And, so I don't know it -- later she was more laughing or crying, of course, than --
Yeah. Then maybe --
-- saying she can't -- what's that saying she used to say, can't -- I can't stop laughing for crying or something.
